questions.question: Dadabhai Naoroji was a _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Businessman**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 **Dadabhai Naoroji **was a businessman and a **great publicist who settled in London.**
 
 
• 
 He was the **first Asian to become a British Member of Parliament** when he was elected to the** House of Commons in 1892.**
 
 
• 
 He formed the** London India Society in 1865 **to put forth views on **Indian political, social and literary subjects.**
 
 
• 
 He also** founded the East India Association in 1867 **with the purpose of putting across Indian viewpoints across to the British public.
 
 
• 
 **He was the President of the Congress Party in 1886, 1893 and 1906.**
 
 
• 
 
**Naoroji’s book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India **offered scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule.

• He estimated a National Income of** Rs. 340 crores and per capita income of Rs.20 in the year 1867-68.**
 
• ​He was also known as the** Indian Gladstone and Grand Old Man of India.**
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the House of Commons on a Liberal Party ticket.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution talks about a uniform civil code?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• **Article 44 talks about a uniform civil code in India.**
 
• A uniform civil code is a proposal to replace personal laws based on religion with a common set of laws for all citizens irrespective of their religion.
 
• This would ensure gender equality and social justice.
 
• 'Uniform Civil Code' is explicitly mentioned in Part 4, Article 44 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• Article 44 says, “The State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
 
• ”Uniform Civil Code is a proposal in India to formulate and implement secular personal laws of citizens which apply on all citizens equally regardless of their religion.
 
• Currently, the personal laws of various communities are governed by their religious scriptures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 352 **is related to the proclamation of emergency, while Article 14 talks about equality before the law and equal protection of laws for all citizens.
 
• **Article 370 **is related to the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The debate over a uniform civil code is ongoing, and it remains to be seen whether it will be implemented in the future.

questions.question:
While burning hydrocarbon fuels, if we see a yellow flame with lots of black smoke, it means that the fuel is

I. made of saturated hydrocarbons.

II. made of unsaturated hydrocarbons.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Hydrocarbon fuel **is fuel that is** derived from a hydrocarbon, which includes gasoline and jet fuel.**
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons give a y**ellow flame **with lots** **of **black smoke **while **saturated hydrocarbons give a clean flame.**
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons** are hydrocarbons that have **double or triple covalent bonds** **between adjacent carbon atoms.**
 
• The colour of the flame is yellow because of the presence of unburnt carbon particles.

Thus, On burning hydrocarbon fuels, we see a yellow flame with lots of black smoke, which indicates that the fuel is **made of unsaturated hydrocarbons.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated hydrocarbo**n is a hydrocarbon in which all the** carbon-carbon bonds are single bonds.**

questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was ____.

All India Trade Union Congress:

__
 
• The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) is the oldest trade union federation in India.
 
• It is associated with the Communist Party of India.
 
• According to provisional statistics from the Ministry of Labour, AITUC had a membership of 14.2 million in 2013.
 
• It was founded on 31 October 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.
 
• Until 1945 when unions became organised on party lines, it was the primary trade union organisation in India.
 
• The main purpose of labour unions is to give workers the power to negotiate for more favourable working conditions and other benefits through collective bargaining.
 
• The following are the objectives of a trade union:
 
 
• To improve the economic lot of workers by securing them better wages.
 
• To secure workers better working conditions.
 
• To secure bonuses for the workers from the profits of the enterprise/organization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• C. Rajagopalachari (1878-1972) was an Indian lawyer, writer and independence activist.
 
• He was popular as **Rajaji, C.R. and Mootharignar Rajaji.**
 
• He was the **last Governor-General **before India became a republic.
 
• He is remembered for his contribution to the independence struggle as well as his intellectual and administrative prowess.
 
• **In 1954, he was honoured with India’s highest civilian award, Bharat Ratna.**
 
 
 
• **Chandra Shekhar Azad**
 
 
• ​Azad was born on 23rd July 1906 in the Alirajpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Chandra Shekhar, then a 15-year-old student, joined a Non-Cooperation Movement in December 1921. As a result, he was arrested.
 
• On being presented before a magistrate, he gave his name as "Azad" (The Free), his father's name as "Swatantrata" (Independence) and his residence as "Jail". Therefore, he came to be known as Chandra Shekhar Azad.
 
• After the suspension of the non-cooperation movement in 1922 by Gandhi, Azad joined Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
• Most of the fund collection for revolutionary activities was done through robberies of government property. In line with the same, Kakori Train Robbery near Kakori, Lucknow was done in 1925 by HRA.
 
• He died at Azad Park in Allahabad on 27th February 1931.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**
 
 
• **​**Pandit Motilal Nehru was a lawyer and politician who was born in the year 1861.
 
• He was elected to United Provinces Council__ in 1909.
 
• He was contemporary of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
 
• He attended the **Delhi Durbar in 1911 **in honour of the visit of King George V.
 
• Motilal was elected **President of the United Province Congress in the year 1911**.

questions.question: The tertiary sector of Indian Economy is related to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__transport, communication and business/services__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tertiary sectors** are activities** that help in the development of the primary and secondary sectors.**
 
• The tertiary sector is often known as the **service industry.**
 
• It makes the most contribution to India's GDP, **more than 50%.**
 
• The tertiary sector is made up of the market services sector and the non-market services sector.
 
• Examples of Tertiary Sector
 
 
• **Trade, Hotels, and Restaurants**
 
• **Real estate and Business services**
 
• **Transport, Storage, and Communication**
 
• **Financial services such as Banking, Insurance, etc.**
 
• **Real estate and Business services**
 
• **Public Administration**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary sector**

 
 
• The primary sector of the economy uses** natural resources directly for its livelihood.**
 
• For eg Agriculture, forestry, and fishing, as well as mining and oil and gas extraction etc. 
 
• Examples of Primary Sector are:
 
 
• **Farming**
 
• **Fishing**
 
• **Coal mining**
 
• **Forestry and logging**
 
• **Oil extraction**
 
• **Diamond mining**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Secondary sector**
 
 
• ​The secondary sector of the economy comprises businesses that produce a finished, useful product.
 
• It** depends on primary sector companies** for raw materials. 
 
• Mining, manufacturing, and construction are all part of this industry.
 
• The secondary sector** contributes 24% of the share in the Indian economy.**

questions.question: Mushroom rocks are formed due to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**wind erosion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A mushroom rock **also called a **rock pedestal**, or **a pedestal rock **is a **naturally occurring rock **whose **shape**, as its **name implies**, **resembles a mushroom**.
 
• **The rocks are deformed **in a **number of different ways**: **by erosion and weathering**, **glacial action**, or a **sudden disturbance**. **Mushroom rocks **are **related to**, but **different from, yardang**.
 
• **A mushroom rock**, rock pedestal, or gour is a typical **mushroom-shaped landform **that is formed **by the action of wind erosion**.
 
• It's an **average height **of **two to three feet **(**0.6 to 0.9 m**) from **the base**.
 
• **Wind erosion **is a **natural process **that moves the **soil from one location **to **another by wind power**. It can **cause significant economic and environmental damage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debris **in the **glacial environment **may be **deposited directly by the ice **(till) or, after **reworking**, by **meltwater streams **(outwash). The **resulting deposits **are **termed glacial drift**.
 
• **Deposition occurs **where **waves **and **other ocean motions slow**. The **smallest particles**, such as silt and clay, are **deposited away from the shore**. **Larger particles **are **deposited on the beach**.
 
• **Heavy rainfall **or the **melting of snow **creates **running water **which **removes soil by sheet**, **rill**, or **gully erosion**. Rill **erosion **occurs in **discrete streamlets carved into the soil**. When rills **become too deep **to **be removed by plowing**, **gullies form**.

questions.question: The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple was constructed in 999 A.D. by the king Dhangadeva of ___________ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandela.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** was constructed by** King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty in 999 A.D.**
 
• **The Chandela dynasty** ruled in central India from the **9th to the 13th century **and was known for their patronage of art and architecture, particularly the erotic sculptures on their temples.
 
• It's **part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments**, a UNESCO World Heritage site, located in **Madhya Pradesh, Central India.**
 
• The Chandela dynasty was known for its art and architecture, and **among their 85 original temples, around 22 survive today **and reflect the height of the North Indian art form known as** 'Nagara'.**
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is **dedicated to Lord Shiva **and houses a linga in the main shrine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pala dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in eastern India from the 8th to the 12th century, known for their patronage of Buddhism and the Nalanda University.
 
• **The Pallava dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in southern India from the 3rd to the 9th century, known for their patronage of art, literature, and architecture, particularly the Shore Temple in Mahabalipuram.
 
• **The Chola dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in southern India from the 9th to the 13th century, known for their naval power, trade, and patronage of art and architecture, particularly the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur.

questions.question: Liver gland secretes ________ that is stored in a sac called the gall bladder.

questions.solution:

• The general definition of the public sector includes government ownership or control rather than mere function and thereby includes, for example, the exercise of public authority or the implementation of public policy. 
 
• PSUs (Public Sector Undertakings) are government-owned corporations in India, in which 51% or more than 51% of the paid-up share capital is owned by the government of India.

questions.question: ‘Ashtadhyayi’, written by Sanskrit scholar Panini, is a book on ______.

questions.question: Unemployment arising due to mismatch between Job availability in the market and skills of available worker is called?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Structural**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term unemployment refers to a situation where a person **actively searches for employment but is unable **to find work.
 
• **Structural **unemployment comes about through a **technological change in the structure of the economy** in which labour markets operate. 
 
• Technological changes can lead to unemployment among workers displaced from jobs that are no longer needed
 
• Examples of such changes include the replacement of horse-drawn transport with automobiles and the automation of manufacturing,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional Unemployment**

 
 
• This type of unemployment is usually short-lived. It is also the least problematic from an economic standpoint. It occurs when people voluntarily change jobs.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal unemployment**
 
 
• It occurs at different points over the year because of seasonal patterns that affect jobs. Some examples include ski instructors, fruit pickers and holiday-related jobs.
 
 
 
• **Economic Unemployment**
 
 
• During an economic downturn, a shortfall of demand for goods and services results in a lack of jobs available for those who want to work. Businesses experiencing weaker demand might reduce the number of people they employ by laying off existing workers or hiring fewer new workers.

questions.question: The bill which provide for the trial of British or European person by Indians was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ilbert Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 'Ilbert Bill' was introduced in 1883 under the Viceroyship of Lord Ripon.

 
 
• Ilbert Bill was drafted by Sir Courtenay Ilbert on 9th February 1883 during the viceroyship of Lord Rippon.
 
• The main objective behind the introduction of this bill is to allow Indian judges to try cases in session courts involving Britishers.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The introduction of the bill had roused anger and resentment among people, especially English women and British tea and indigo planters in Bengal.
 
• English women argued that Bengali women were not respected by their male counterparts, so they shouldn't get the power to try cases involving Britishers.
 
• On the contrary, Bengali women who supported the bill said that they were more educated and had good academic records than English Women.

questions.question: As per census 2011, which among the following Union Territories of India has least population density per square kilometre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the** census 2011, Andaman and Nicobar **Islands has the** least population density** per square kilometre among all the Union Territories of India.
 
• The population density of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is **46 persons** per square kilometre, which is much** lower **than the** national average **of **382 persons **per square kilometre.
 
• The** low population density** of Andaman and Nicobar Islands can be attributed to its** geographical location**, as it is situated far away from the **mainland **and comprises of a **group of islands.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jammu and Kashmir **has a population density of **56 persons per square kilometre,** which is **higher **than Andaman and Nicobar Islands but still **lower** than the national average.
 
• **Chandigarh **has a population density of **9,252 persons** per square kilometre, which is one of the **highest **among all the Union Territories of India.
 
• **Delhi **has a population density of **11,320 persons** per square kilometre, which is **the ****highest **among all the Union Territories of India.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** option 2.**

questions.question: Prithviraja III defeated an Afghan ruler named ______ in 1191.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sultan Muhammad Ghori**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The best-known Chahamana ruler was Prithviraj III (1168- 1192), who defeated an Afghan ruler named Sultan Muhammad Ghori in 1191, but lost to him the very next year, in 1192.
 
• Mohammad Ghori’s invasion (1175 AD-1206 AD):
 
 
• Mohammad Ghori invaded India and laid the foundation of Muslim domination in India.
 
• He is often considered the founder of Muslim rule in India.
 
 

 
• Battle of Tarain:

 
 
• In the first battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 the Ghori Forces were completely rooted out by Prithviraj Chauhan.
 
• The second battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 in which Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Ghori.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Prithviraja III

 
• Prithviraja III was the best-known Chahamana ruler.
 
• From 1177 to 1192 CE, Prithviraja III, sometimes referred to as Prithviraj Chauhan or Rai Pithora, ruled Sapadalaksha.
 
• He belonged to the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty, and his capital was Ajmer in modern-day Rajasthan. In 1177 CE, when Prithviraj ascended the throne as a boy, he inherited a kingdom that ran from Thanesar in the north to Jahazpur (Mewar) in the south.
 
• He sought to enlarge this realm by engaging in military operations against nearby countries, most notably by defeating the Chandelas.

questions.question: Which of the following is not attracted by magnet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When we mix **zinc **and **copper **to make the **alloy brass**, by the process we get a non-magnetic material. Therefore brass is not magnetic.
 
• Ferromagnetic substances are those which develop strong magnetization in the direction of the magnetizing field.
 
• They are strongly attracted by a magnet and tend to move from the weaker to the stronger part of a magnetic field.
 
• Magnetic susceptibility is very large and positive i.e. χ > 1000
 
• **Examples of magnetic properties**: Iron, cobalt, nickel, gadolinium, and alloys like alnico.
 
• ​Thus in their natural states, metals such as brass, copper, zink, gold, and silver will not attract magnets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A metal is said to possess magnetic property, if it is attracted by a magnet.
 
• Almost all ferrous metals, excepting some types of stainless steel, can be attracted by a magnet and all non-ferrous metals and their alloys will not be attracted by a magnet.
 
• Certain metals in their natural states such as **aluminium**, **copper**, **brass**, **lead, gold**, and **silver **don't attract magnets due to the fact they are weak metals
